title: Crane Wire Rope Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.1413)
subtitle: For shift, monthly and annual wire rope inspections on cranes and derricks under Subpart CC.
instructions: Mark each item OK, Defect or N/A.
Report any Defect at once to the competent or qualified person running the inspection; 1926.1413(a)(4) and (c)(3) set when the rope must come out of service.
The rope manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks.

sections.title: Shift inspection and critical review items
items: Competent person began the visual inspection before the shift and finished it during or before the shift
All running and standing ropes likely to be used this shift were observed
Rotation resistant rope in use was examined closely
Boom hoist and luffing hoist rope
Rope checked along its length, especially at reverse bends
Rope at flange, crossover and repetitive pickup points on drums checked
Rope at or near terminal ends checked
Rope touching saddles, equalizer sheaves or limited-travel sheaves checked

sections.title: Category I and Category III deficiencies
items: No significant kinking, crushing, unstranding, birdcaging, core failure signs or steel core protruding between outer strands
No significant corrosion on the rope
No electric arc damage from a non-power-line source and no heat damage
End connections not significantly corroded, cracked, bent or worn
No core protrusion or other distortion showing core failure
Rope has had no prior electrical contact with a power line
No broken strand anywhere on the rope

sections.title: Category II broken wires and diameter
items: Fewer than six random broken wires per lay and fewer than three broken wires in any one strand per lay
Fewer than two random broken wires per six rope diameters and fewer than four per 30 rope diameters
No more than two broken wires per lay beyond end connections and no more than one per lay at an end connection
Reduction from nominal diameter is 5% or less

sections.title: Removal from service and repair
items: Competent person made an immediate safety-hazard determination for each Category I finding
Category II rope out of use
Rope not used until the manufacturer's removal criterion is met, the rope is replaced, or a localized section is severed out
Category III rope out of use
Rope not used until replaced, or until a localized defect other than power line contact is severed out
No lengths of rope joined by splicing
Rope that touched an energized power line has not been repaired
Two wraps remain on the drum with the load and/or boom at its lowest position
Equipment or the affected hoist tagged out per 1926.1417(f)(1) until the rope is repaired or replaced

sections.title: Monthly, annual, lubricant and records
items: Inspection to paragraph (a) done this month
Deficiencies flagged for monitoring at the annual inspection were checked
Qualified person inspected ropes in use to paragraph (a) within the last 12 months
Complete and thorough check of the rope surface along its entire length done within the 12-month period
Lubricant on the rope does not hinder inspection
Inspection documents available to all inspectors during the retention period

references: 29 CFR 1926.1413: Wire rope—inspection (Part 1926 Subpart CC, Cranes and Derricks in Construction)
